title: My weekday routine
instructions: Write a paragraph about a normal weekday. Say what you do in the morning, afternoon and evening, and one thing that is different this week.
checklist: Use the present simple for habits
Use the present continuous for this week
Use time expressions (in the morning, at 7, on Monday)
Use at least 3 linking words (first, then, after that…)
modelAnswer: On weekdays, I usually wake up at 5:30. First, I have a shower and get dressed. Then I have a quick breakfast and leave home at 6:45 because the traffic is terrible during rush hour. I start work at 8 o'clock. In the afternoon, I usually have meetings with my team. I get home at about 7 p.m. After dinner, I study English for thirty minutes and I go to bed at 11. This week is different because I'm preparing an important presentation, so I'm staying late at the office.

title: Email to a colleague: changing a meeting
instructions: Write an email to a colleague. Say you can't come to the meeting on Thursday, explain why, and suggest another day and time.
checklist: Greeting and closing
Reason (because…)
A suggestion (Could we… ? / How about…?)
Polite tone
modelAnswer:
Hi Sarah,

I'm sorry, but I can't come to the meeting on Thursday at 10. I have to visit a client in Kpalimé that day and I will not be back before the evening.

Could we meet on Friday morning instead? I'm free from 9 to 12. If that doesn't work for you, Monday afternoon is also possible.

Thanks for understanding.

Best regards,
Koffi

title: A difficult situation you solved
instructions: Describe a difficult situation you experienced at work or at school. Explain what happened, what you did and what you learned.
checklist: Past simple and past continuous for the story
A clear beginning, middle and end
What you learned (present perfect is useful: I have learned…)
Linking words: at first, then, finally, as a result
usefulLanguage: At first, I didn't know what to do.
modelAnswer:
A few months ago, I was working on a website for a client when the server suddenly crashed, two days before the launch. At first, I panicked, because we had no recent backup of the database.

Then I decided to stay calm and make a plan. I called the hosting company, explained the problem clearly and asked them to restore the latest snapshot. While they were working on it, I informed the client honestly about the delay. Finally, the site was restored and we launched only one day late.

As a result, the client trusted us even more because we had communicated well. Since then, I have set up automatic daily backups for every project, and I have learned that clear communication is as important as technical skills.

title: Opinion: should university be free?
instructions: Some people think university education should be free for everyone. Do you agree or disagree? Give reasons and examples.
checklist: Introduction with a clear opinion
Two body paragraphs, each with one main idea + example
One opposing view (However, some people argue…)
Conclusion that repeats your opinion in new words
modelAnswer:
Many people believe that university should be free for everyone. In my opinion, free higher education is a good idea, although it must be organised carefully.

Firstly, free university gives equal opportunities. Talented students from poor families often stop studying because they cannot pay tuition fees. If university were free, the country would benefit from all its talent, not only from the richest families.

Secondly, a more educated population helps the economy. For example, countries with high levels of education usually have more innovative companies and better-paid jobs.

However, some people argue that free education is too expensive for the government and that students may not take their studies seriously. This is a fair point. One solution could be to offer free education with conditions, such as passing every year.

In conclusion, I believe that free university is a valuable investment, as long as the system rewards effort and is financially realistic.

title: IELTS Task 2: studying abroad
instructions: Some people believe that studying abroad is the best way to prepare for a successful career, while others think that studying in your own country is more valuable. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Introduction: paraphrase the question and state your opinion
Body 1: the first view, with an explanation and an example
Body 2: the second view, with an explanation and an example
Use contrast linkers (whereas, although, nevertheless)
Conclusion: summarise both sides and restate your opinion
usefulLanguage: Proponents of this view claim that…
To sum up, while… , I firmly believe that…
modelAnswer:
In an increasingly global job market, many students wonder whether they should complete their education abroad or at home. Although both options have clear advantages, I believe that studying abroad offers more for a future career, provided that students plan it carefully.

Proponents of studying abroad argue that it develops skills that employers value highly. Living in another country forces students to become independent, to adapt to new situations and to communicate in a foreign language every day. For example, a Togolese student who completes a master's degree in Canada will not only become fluent in English but will also build an international network that may lead to job offers.

On the other hand, studying in one's own country has significant benefits. It is considerably cheaper, which means that students and their families avoid heavy debts. Moreover, local universities understand the national economy, so graduates may find it easier to obtain jobs in local companies or public institutions. Some people also maintain that talented graduates are needed at home to develop their country.

From my perspective, the experience of living abroad is extremely valuable, although it is not the only route to success. The most effective approach might be to combine both: completing a first degree at home and then spending a year or a master's programme abroad. Nevertheless, the decision should depend on each student's financial situation and career goals.

To sum up, while studying at home is affordable and locally relevant, studying abroad provides language skills, independence and international contacts. For these reasons, I firmly believe it is the better preparation for a successful career.

title: C1 essay: technology and learning
instructions: "Artificial intelligence will make traditional teachers unnecessary within a generation." To what extent do you agree or disagree? Support your answer with reasons and examples.
checklist: Nuanced thesis (to what extent)
Hedging: may, arguably, to some extent
At least one inversion or cleft for emphasis
Nominalised phrases in topic sentences
A concession and a rebuttal
Conclusion that answers the question precisely
usefulLanguage: It would be naive to assume that…
Not only does AI…, but it also…
While there is some merit in this view, …
modelAnswer:
The rapid spread of artificial intelligence in education has led some commentators to predict the disappearance of the teaching profession. While AI will undoubtedly transform how people learn, I would argue that the claim that teachers will become unnecessary within a generation significantly overstates what the technology can do.

There is, admittedly, some merit in the optimistic view. Not only can AI tutors adapt instantly to each learner's level, but they are also available at any hour and at negligible cost. For students in regions with a severe shortage of qualified teachers, this could arguably be the most significant improvement in access to education in decades. A learner in a rural area could, for instance, receive individual feedback on an essay within seconds.

What is often overlooked, however, is that learning is not merely the transmission of information. Research suggests that students who depend on AI for answers tend to perform worse in later assessments, as the tool removes the effortful practice through which lasting understanding develops. Moreover, the motivation of reluctant learners, the management of group dynamics and the modelling of curiosity remain distinctly human tasks. It is precisely these aspects of teaching that determine whether students persevere.

It seems far more plausible, therefore, that the role of teachers will evolve rather than vanish. Teachers may spend less time correcting routine exercises and more time designing projects, mentoring and helping students use AI critically.

On balance, AI is likely to become a powerful assistant in classrooms, but the expectation that it will replace teachers within a generation is, in my view, unrealistic. The real challenge lies in ensuring that technology strengthens, rather than erodes, the skills that education exists to develop.
